text:
The Jets are 13-9-4 and 8-1-1 in their last ten, and they are doing it without Connor Hellebuyck, who asked out and is now with New Jersey. Stuart Skinner, signed as a free agent from Pittsburgh, has taken the net; he made 34 saves against Utah while Gabriel Vilardi scored a hat trick. Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press wrote about how that ten-game run changed the narrative of the season.

The underlying numbers are more modest. Winnipeg gets 48.5% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) and our numbers say the Jets have about 3.4 more points than their play has earned. Playoff odds: 38%. The defense is the concern, and it just got thinner: Dylan DeMelo is out four to six weeks with a lower-body injury.

The headline is Mark Scheifele, who passed Dale Hawerchuk to become the franchise's all-time leading goal scorer, and who has 19 points in his last ten, above the 12.3 his chances suggest. He and Kyle Connor have played almost every minute together, with Vilardi or Cole Perfetti on the other side, outscoring opponents 13-9 with Vilardi. Dawson Mercer is running hot too. The question Sportsnaut raised is the right one: Hellebuyck used to hide the Jets' defensive problems, and now Connor's scoring is doing it. Scoring this hot doesn't usually last.
headline: Life after Hellebuyck is going better than expected
